newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam assembly members seek say on cabinet posts.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam assembly members seek say on cabinet posts.

text.p: Two members of Vietnam's traditionally compliant National Assembly have called for cabinet members to explain allegations of corruption in their ministries.

Wednesday's Quan Doi Nhan Dan (People's Army) newspaper quoted Dinh Uong, from central Vietnam's Quang Ngai province, and Nguyen Trong Nhan, from an area close to Hanoi, as saying ministers should present their cases to the assembly before a planned reshuffle.
They added that the top-lawmaking body should then be given a say in the new cabinet line-up, which is expected to be announced in a matter of days or weeks.

"It's also necessary to avoid the situation where personnel changes are announced so close to the day when the National Assembly gives approval, that the collective is unable to make a contribution," it quoted them as saying.
Vietnam's National Assembly, which meets twice a year, functions to ratify decisions made by the top leadership.
But observers say the lawmaking body has begun demonstrating a previously unseen capacity for debate in recent years.
Changes to the cabinet are widely expected at ministries with economic portfolios as well as at the powerful Interior (Police) Ministry.
